subject: multigroup PCM with constrained intercepts - fscores() outputs different latent score estimate based on group

messages.author: fce58c3d4618fa13
messages.subject: multigroup PCM with constrained intercepts - fscores() outputs different latent score estimate based on group
parts:
Hi, Phil,

I came upon the following problem:

I have estimated a unidimensional multigroup partial credit model (well, a portion of the items are only 2 categories, but most are up to 4 categories) on five groups, but kept the intercepts constrained to be equal across groups, so that only the latent means and variances could differ between the groups. 

Now, I have an additional vector of scores that I want to score:


load('expmodel.Rdata') # Load the model
load('trialdata.Rdata') # Load the vector of data

And let's say I want to estimate the latent score from this vector. I have to extract one of the group models from the original multigroup model and use it as an argument in fscores(), like so:

# group number 1
group.x <- extract.group(expmodelgroup, 1)

fscores(group.x, full.scores.SE = T, method = 'ML',
        response.pattern = trialdata)[48]

[1] 0.9088377

If I do the same thing using another of the group models, I get a different result:

# group number 5
group.x <- extract.group(expmodelgroup, 5)

fscores(group.x, full.scores.SE = T, method = 'ML',
        response.pattern = trialdata)[48]

[1] 0.5523227

...although the only parameters that should differ between the group models are the latent mean and variance estimates. However, since I'm using the Maximum Likelihood method in fscores(), even this should not make a difference. What am I missing? 

Find the model and data objects attached for reproducibility. Thanks a lot for answering!



P.S.: Is there a way to contribute to the development of mirt? I figured I could lend a hand if possible ;)

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multigroup PCM with constrained intercepts - fscores() outputs different latent score estimate based on group
parts:
Sorry for the late reply. This does appear to be a potential bug, and one that I can't say I've thought hard about. The extract.group() function was largely built as a secondary tool of interest, and I don't recall ever trying to re-organize the data structure to make it seem as though a real single-group model were constructed (multi-group data structures include some missing frequency counts in order to keep the response category counts consistent). If you'd prefer, feel free to open an issue on Github and we can track the issue better there. Otherwise, if you are comfortable with the version control Git, you could sent a pull-request on Github with your potential solution if you have one in mind. Thanks.

Phil

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: multigroup PCM with constrained intercepts - fscores() outputs different latent score estimate based on group
parts:
No need, I just patched the issue. Turns out I didn't pass the required 'mins' internal to indicate what constitutes the lowest category in polytomous items (sometimes its 0, sometimes 1....but it could be anything). This created the incorrect dummy matrices internally, which is why the results were inconsistent with the ML estimator. The latest dev now provides .908..... for both inputs after using the corrected extract.group() function. Thanks for the report!

Phil
